Hi Jordan / Acme legal — following up with the artifacts Marissa requested. TL;DR: Acme = Controller, Redwood = Processor is the correct alignment for your stated flows; recommend Processor-to-Controller SCC module where required. See details below and attached files.

What I'm attaching
- Redwood_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf — our latest SOC 2 Type II (covers security and availability controls).
- SCC_Comparison.xlsx — a short matrix comparing SCC modules and when we recommend each.
- Draft_DPA_Redwood_v1.pdf — our standard DPA (editable).

Key points
- Controller/Processor: Based on your statement that Acme controls which customer data is submitted and how it is used, Acme is Controller. Redwood processes per your instructions and stores debug logs only for 30 days by default. We can include a configurable retention clause in the DPA.
- SCC module: For transfers out of the EU, we recommend Processor-to-Controller SCCs (Module 2 variant) when the processor acts under instructions. If Acme is transferring data to downstream subprocessors in a Controller role, we can discuss Processor-to-Processor where appropriate. See SCC_Comparison.xlsx for decision tree.
- Onboarding evidence: we can provide our SOC2 report and a completed vendor security questionnaire. If you prefer, we can fill your questionnaire (attached as ACME_DPA_Request.pdf) and return it with evidence.
